summary.headline: The Planning Board recommended temporary occupancy for Fay School, approved National Grid's vegetation plan, and discussed draft two-family zoning amendments.
summary.summary: The Planning Board paid tribute to longtime former chair Charlie Gaffney before addressing site plan compliance for Fay School's building addition at 25 Middle Road. The board voted to recommend a 90-day temporary certificate of occupancy for Fay School with conditions requiring a mitigation plan for removed trees and non-native landscaping. In a joint session with the tree warden, the board approved National Grid's fiscal year 2027 vegetation management plan for power line tree trimming. Members also reviewed proposed zoning bylaw amendments from the Zoning Board of Appeals to remove the two-year waiting requirement for two-family home conversions ahead of a September public hearing.

topics.title: Tribute to former Planning Board Chair Charlie Gaffney
topics.summary: Former Planning Board colleagues and community members remembered Charlie Gaffney, a longtime Planning Board chair who recently passed away. Speakers reflected on his decades of civic dedication, his advocacy for town character during major commercial development, and his welcoming mentorship of fellow board members.
key_details: Former board members shared memories of Gaffney's leadership during significant town development in the 1980s and 1990s.
Gaffney was recalled for his deep affection for the town and his consistent presence at town government proceedings.
topics.outcome: Memorial remarks concluded and condolences were offered to his family.

topics.title: Fay School building addition as-builts and temporary occupancy (25 Middle Road)
topics.summary: Representatives for Fay School presented as-built drawings and requested a recommendation for a temporary certificate of occupancy for an addition at 25 Middle Road. The discussion addressed discrepancies between the approved plans and construction, including three trees removed for a drainage line, reduced site lighting, and non-native landscape substitutions. The board approved recommending temporary occupancy provided the school submits a tree and native planting mitigation plan within 90 days.
key_details: The project involves a roughly 9,200-square-foot building addition that recently completed construction.
Three mature trees were removed to install a 36-inch drainage pipe, and only two of three required eastern redbud trees were planted.
Contractors inadvertently installed non-native species from an outdated plan, and full replacement would cost an estimated $25,000 to $30,000.
Site lighting was reduced by omitting three light poles and two wall sconces to control light spill and project costs.
Peer review by Foth and O'Neill and certifications from Nitsch Engineering will be finalized to confirm drainage system function.
topics.outcome: The board voted 3-0 to recommend issuance of a temporary certificate of occupancy subject to a 90-day mitigation plan for trees and native plantings.

topics.title: 22 Turnpike Road site plan modification continued hearing
topics.summary: Engineer Peter Bemis presented revised site modification plans for 22 Turnpike Road responding to town peer review comments. The revisions double the size of an underground stormwater infiltration system and accommodate previously unpermitted patios and a storage shed. Board members reviewed lighting plans that exceed normal residential limits due to sports recreation use and directed the applicant to submit a formal waiver request.
key_details: The stormwater infiltration system capacity was doubled to meet peer review standards.
Plans were updated to document existing patios and a storage shed constructed behind the driving range.
Lighting plans seek to replace metal halide fixtures with LEDs under commercial sports facility lighting standards.
The applicant must file a formal lighting waiver letter citing sports lighting criteria before the next meeting.
topics.outcome: The public hearing was continued to September 14, 2026.

topics.title: National Grid FY27 Vegetation Management Plan
topics.summary: The board held a joint session with the town tree warden to review National Grid's annual vegetation management plan for fiscal year 2027. National Grid's representative outlined standard pruning along distribution circuits that run into Southborough from Marlboro. The board and tree warden approved the plan, with pruning anticipated to begin within a few weeks.
key_details: Pruning will occur along circuits 10, 11, and 12, affecting Parmenter Road, Pine Hill Road, Nichols Street, and Clemmons Street.
Clearance specifications require 15 feet above wires, 6 feet to the sides, and 10 feet below.
No full tree removals are included in the routine distribution trimming plan; hazardous trees will be handled separately through joint hearings.
Contractor Northern Tree will conduct customer notifications and provide daily email schedules to the town and police.
topics.outcome: The Planning Board voted 3-0 and the tree warden concurred to approve the FY27 vegetation management plan.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The board deferred discussion on Master Plan Implementation Committee goals due to member absences. Members also approved the draft meeting minutes from July 13, 2026, and adjourned the meeting.
key_details: Review of Master Plan goals was tabled until a full board is present.
Meeting minutes from July 13, 2026, were approved.

topics.title: Town planner report and project updates
topics.summary: The town planner reviewed ongoing town development matters and municipal dates. Updates included upcoming meetings for a potential Costco development, parking studies for the Fayville Park expansion, and Fay School athletic field changes. The Select Board has formally scheduled a Special Town Meeting for Saturday, October 17, 2026.
key_details: A pre-application meeting with Costco representatives is scheduled for August 24, 2026.
The Fayville Park expansion parking study will be discussed jointly on August 27 and brought to the Select Board on September 2.
Special Town Meeting was scheduled by the Select Board for Saturday, October 17, 2026, at 10 a.m. at Trottier Middle School.
The 20 Southville Road MBTA Communities multi-family proposal is continuing review before the Conservation Commission.
Fay School plans to convert two natural grass soccer fields to artificial turf and expand parking near its northern property boundary.

topics.title: ZBA proposed two-family dwelling zoning bylaw amendments
topics.summary: Zoning Board of Appeals member Doris Cahill presented draft zoning amendments intended for the October Special Town Meeting warrant. The proposal eliminates an existing rule requiring a single-family dwelling to exist for at least two years before converting into a two-family dwelling. Planning Board members discussed distinguishing two-family homes from accessory dwelling units and multi-family units, and considered potential impacts on lot coverage and industrial zones.
key_details: Current zoning requires a two-year waiting period between single-family home construction and two-family conversion.
The draft bylaw removes the two-year restriction to allow new construction or conversion to two-family dwellings without delay.
The board discussed clarifying definitions to ensure two-family structures are distinct from accessory dwelling units and multi-family complexes.
Members raised concerns regarding whether two-family properties could simultaneously add an accessory dwelling unit, potentially creating three units on a single lot.
A formal public hearing before the Planning Board is scheduled for September 14, 2026.
topics.outcome: The board provided feedback on the draft language and scheduled a public hearing for September 14, 2026.
topics.why_it_matters: The proposed bylaw would change housing density rules and make it easier to build or convert two-family homes across residential zones.

votes.motion: Recommend issuance of a temporary certificate of occupancy for Fay School at 25 Middle Road with conditions requiring a landscape and tree mitigation plan within 90 days
Approve the National Grid Vegetation Management Plan for fiscal year 2027

public_comment.summary: A resident of Southville Road encouraged Fay School to involve students in planting native species and suggested establishing biodiversity and pollinator gardens to offset removed trees.
A resident of Latisquama Road inquired about town trimming standards versus utility company specifications, expressing concern over the aesthetic impact of roadside tree trimming.
